Philips CAM150BU/37 Waterproof 8 MP Digital Camera with CMOS Sensor and 4 x Optical Zoom (Black) I have to say, I was excited to get this thanks to the zoom for the video, but I was sorely disappointed in its quality. The indoor video I took of my son's music concert, in admittedly relatively low-light (but nowhere near dark) was nearly unwatchable. The focus was terrible and the output was super grainy. My wife, sitting right next to me and thus experiencing the exact same environment, taped the show using our Kodak playsport and it came out absolutely wonderful, well worth sending out to family members. There was simply no comparison between the two. While the sound quality was a closer match, I'd still give the nod to the Kodak over the Phillips. The still photos in the same situation came out just as bad, also grainy, also often blurry, and often washed-out as well. I tried both video and stills at various levels of zoom--without a zoom the quality of both was noticeably better, but still poor quality. I then took stills out in a well-lit hallway and again was disappointed in the quality and again, the Kodak completely outmatched the Phillips.

I've used it in outdoor conditions and better lit conditions and there's no doubt the picture quality is better in those conditions, but in all of them it comes in quite below the Kodak in quality.

Other issues:

The zoom was very slow to auto-focus and took several long seconds before settling in.

the choice of a micro-SD. Not only is it annoyingly different, which I could live with, but it really took some force to get it into the slot. In fact, the first time I used it I left it sticking partway out assuming it was a clever design that shutting the cover would put the card into the slot as it needed to go. This did work--the card obviously slipped in and had no issues--but then, when I needed to connect it to the computer to download, which necessitates leaving the cover open for the cable, I realized what I had thought was a clever design wasn't purposeful, as I needed to get the card all the way in. I eventually used a pen cap to push it in, wincing at the pressure needed to do so. (I won't discuss the times it popped out and I had to search on the floor/desk for it).

it has its pluses, but to be honest, since its primary purpose is taking good pictures and video, and so far it hasn't, I don't see the point in outlining the good points which are so secondary to its primary objective.

I'll use it a few more times to ensure this review is a fair one, but there is no way I will do so at special events or without using the Kodak as backup (or one of my point-and-shoots which also shoot far better video based on the samples so far--two Canon elphs and our larger Canon IS). At this point, not only would I not use this but I wouldn't give it to a friend. But as mentioned, I'll give it a few more chances and report back.
text_fidelity_b: Philips CAM150BU/37 Waterproof 8 MP Digital Camera with CMOS Sensor and 4 x Optical Zoom (Black)

LeadsaiL Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Wireless USB Mouse and Computer Keyboard Set, Compact and Silent for Windows Laptop, Desktop, PC Short of both units having an internal rechargeable battery with wired use option (while charging), this set has about everything I can imagine wanting out of a keyboard and mouse combo:

1. Actually a combo, so I only need one transmitter when I want to use my docking station with my laptop.

2. Both units have power switches. While it's annoying to turn them off after each use, at least you can be sure the batteries aren't draining needlessly.

3. USB receiver hides securely on board the mouse so it shouldn't get lost easily.

4. Keyboard is full and not missing any buttons as far as I can tell. The arrow keys are smushed up, so you may not want this if you actually use those a lot. Backspace and delete have a slightly different relationship than usual. Even so, this is about as small as you can make a full keyboard, and I like compact for this, because generally if I'm using this, I have two computers going at once (other is wired and for the primary dock at the desk).

Also...both look good and feel good. Keyboard has a built in bump in the back where the batteries go. Would love to have rechargeable or even solar powered set up here, but your AAs should last quite a while (and, admittedly, those can be rechargeable).
